newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget vote not likely til Monday-Daschle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget vote not likely til Monday-Daschle.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said he did not think Congress would vote on a catchall spending bill until Monday but he expected lawmakers to act quickly enough to avoid a possible government shutdown.

Republican lawmakers and the White House are working out the final details of a broad spending bill needed to fund a host of government agencies in fiscal 1997, which begins Oct 1, for which regular spending bills have not yet been passed.
Daschle said negotiators were making "reasonably good progress" but still had at least several hours of talks ahead.
"My expectation is we probably won't be able to look at it and vote on it at least until Monday," Daschle said.
Daschle said he believed both Democrats and Republicans were determined to avoid a government shutdown, saying "I think that it's highly unlikely."

Daschle said the latest report he had received about the ongoing negotiations between the White House and Republicans was that the parties were making "reasonably good progress" but that it would require at least several hours of additional talks to work out a final deal.
